text:
### Observed differences

- The routing out of **A08** flipped completely: in the earlier window its observed outgoing transitions went to A13 (about 53%) and A04 (about 47%) across 32 observed transitions; in the later window they go to A16 (about 51%) and A17 (about 49%) across 104 observed transitions. [DIR004]
- **A16** always led back to A05 in the earlier window (62 observed transitions); in the later window it always leads back to A08 (53 observed transitions). [DIR007]
- **A04 and A13 stopped leading to A05 and now lead to A08.** Before, about 28% of A04's and of A13's outgoing transitions went to A05; later, none do — A04 now leads to A13 (about 55%), A07 (about 21%) and A08 (about 23%), and A13 leads to A04 (about 45%), A07 (about 31%) and A08 (about 24%). [DIR002, DIR006]
- **A09** sent about 43% of its observed outgoing transitions to A08 before; later, none do and about 51% go to A05. [DIR005]
- **A05 receded sharply and was rewired:** it appeared in about 21 in 100 traces before (mean 0.68 occurrences per trace) versus about 6 in 100 later (mean 0.13); its outgoing transitions, previously to A16 (about 46%) and A01 (about 54%), now go to A13 (about 54%) and A04 (about 46%). [OCC003, DIR003]
- **A17 appeared and A01 detached from the cycle.** A17 was not observed before; later it appears in about 13 in 100 traces (median position about 0.7 into the trace) and all 51 of its observed outgoing transitions lead to A09. A01's only observed outgoing transition before was A01 → A09 (74 observed); later no outgoing transition from A01 is observed, A01 sits at the first recorded position in every trace containing it (median position about 0.7 before), and its co-occurrence with A04, A05, A08, A09, A13 and A16 fell from roughly 9–21 in 100 traces to zero — even though A01 itself now appears in more traces (about 34 vs 21 in 100). [DIR008, OCC004, POS002, DIR001, POS001, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007]
- **Lag shifts match this rerouting:** pairs that directly followed each other before (A08→A13, A08→A04, A09→A08, A16→A05) now sit about 4–5 positions apart, while pairs that were 4–5 positions apart before (A13→A08, A04→A08, A05→A04, A05→A13, A09→A05) now follow within about 1–3 positions; several of these rest on fewer than about 15 observed pairs. [LAG009, LAG007, LAG014, LAG002, LAG003, LAG005, LAG016, LAG017, LAG012, LAG011]
- **A02** (about 50 vs 38 in 100 traces) and **A03** (about 29 vs 16) took part in fewer cases in the later window. [OCC001, OCC002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the repeating cycle at the centre of the process was rewired, with A08 and A17 taking over the positions previously carried by A05 and A01. In the earlier window the cycle ran A01 → A09 → A08 → A13/A04 → A05, with a repetition loop between A05 and A16 and closure from A05 back to A01. In the later window, A09 leads to A05, A05 leads to A04/A13, both lead on to A08, and A08 closes the loop through A16 (which always leads back to A08) and through the new A17, which feeds A09; A05's participation collapsed from about 21 to about 6 in 100 traces, A17 rose from unobserved to about 13 in 100, and A01 no longer connects to the cycle at all — no observed successor, first position in its traces, no co-occurrence with any cycle activity — although it appears in more traces than before. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, OCC003, OCC004, POS001, POS002, REL001, REL003]

The volume of qualifying evidence far exceeds what an unchanged process produces: 42 control-flow items qualified against roughly 0.4 expected by chance, and each item's difference exceeds about 99.5 in 100 random re-splits of the pooled data. The rerouting is observed directly in successor profiles backed by dozens of transitions in both windows (A16: 62 transitions to A05 before vs 53 to A08 later; A08: 32 vs 104; A05: 136 vs 26), and the relation, occurrence, position and lag items all describe the same rewiring rather than unrelated differences. [DIR004, DIR007, DIR003, REL001, OCC003, LAG014]

Limitations: all items come from a single control-flow family and many cover the same traces, so they are not independent confirmations; several lag comparisons rest on only 4–7 observed pairs; and an unobserved edge (such as A01 → A09 later) is not proven absent, only not seen in 200 traces. A competing explanation the evidence cannot fully exclude is that only a subset of cases follows the new wiring while old-style executions persist at a rate too low to surface in these samples — the complete disappearance of the old edges (e.g., 74 observed A01 → A09 transitions before, none later) makes a substantial old-style share unlikely but not impossible. [LAG006, LAG004, LAG012, DIR001]

Other differences: A02 (about 50 → 38 in 100 traces) and A03 (about 29 → 16) occurred in fewer cases in the later window [OCC001, OCC002]; among A09's remaining outgoing transitions, the share to A06 fell from about 47% to 33% and the share to A12 rose from about 1% to 8% [DIR005]; A13's share to A07 rose from about 19% to 31% [DIR006].
